messages.author: 8e8e14dc05c49189
messages.subject: Moderated Mediation with Covariate
parts:
Hi all, 

I am trying to fit a moderated mediation model to correspond with the attached diagram, however I am having difficulty including the covariate (child behavior). I know how to include the covariate if I were controlling for it in both a and b paths of the model. 

The code I have is below, but I didn't include the covariate (child behavior). Would any be able to suggest how to include it in this formula? 

mod_cbcl_i <- "# a path
         att_neg_c ~ 1 + a1 * group

         # b paths
         cbcl_int_t ~ 1 + b1 * att_neg_c
         cbcl_int_t ~ b2 * c_sex
         cbcl_int_t ~ b3 * att_sex

         # c prime path 
         cbcl_int_t ~ cp * group

         # index of moderated mediation and conditional indirect effects
         a1b3 := a1 * b3
         maleie := a1 * b1 + a1b3 * 0
         femaleie := a1 * b1 + a1b3 * 1"



I have found several resources online that talk about other moderated mediation models with control variable, but not any for my proposed model. I haven't had a chance to look through all the threads in this forum about moderated mediations, so I apologize if there is an answer already listed here. 



Thank you!

messages.author: 12fdd832cacb825e
messages.subject: Re: Moderated Mediation with Covariate
parts:
Regardless of what's going on in the rest of the model, the most common way to include a covariate in SEM is to regress all other variables on it.

Note that this might get you in trouble with direction of causality.

Pat

         # index of moderated mediation and conditional indirect effects

but it sounds like including the covariate like this might be more common?

att_neg_c ~ 1 + a1 * group + covariate

         # b paths
         cbcl_int_t ~ 1 + b1 * att_neg_c + covariate

# index of moderated mediation and conditional indirect effects
         a1b3 := a1 * b3

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Moderated Mediation with Covariate
parts: I was thinking maybe my code would need to look something like this if I was only including the covariate on one path:

If you only regress your mediator on a covariate, I think your indirect effect would be hard to interpret.  The a path would be the effect of group for anyone with the same level of the covariate, but the b paths would not be interpreted as "controlling for the covariate".  In that case, is the indirect effect interpreted as holding the covariate constant or not?  I would follow Pat's advice and use your second syntax.  

Of course, you also have sex only predicting the outcome, but it is a moderator, so the b path is a conditional rather than marginal effect.  Preacher et al. (2007) described models with only either a or b moderated, and I don't think there is a contradiction there.

http://dx.doi.org/10.1080/00273170701341316
